hints: Follow the incident sound wave to the top end of the tube.
Then identify the returning wave and how it combines with the upward-travelling incident wave.
walkthrough: The incident sound wave travels up the tube and reflects at its top end.
The reflected sound wave travels down the tube, opposite to the incident wave.
The incident and reflected waves overlap and superpose, forming the stationary wave.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the incident sound wave reflects at the top end of the tube.
States that the incident and reflected waves interfere or superpose.

hints: The labelled antinodes at the open ends have maximum oscillation amplitude.
The node at the midpoint has zero amplitude, so use these three fixed positions to shape the graph.
walkthrough: The open ends at h = 0 and h = 0.60 m are antinodes, so the amplitude is maximum at both positions.
The midpoint at h = 0.30 m is a node, so the amplitude is zero there.
Draw a smooth amplitude profile that falls from a maximum at h = 0 to zero at h = 0.30 m, then rises to a maximum at h = 0.60 m.

ai_rubric.observable: Sketches maximum amplitude at h = 0 and h = 0.60 m only.
Sketches minimum or zero amplitude at h = 0.30 m only.

hints: Sound is a longitudinal wave, so air particles oscillate parallel to the direction of wave travel.
The sound wave travels along the tube, whose axis is vertical.
walkthrough: A sound wave is longitudinal, so an air particle oscillates parallel to the direction of propagation.
The tube is vertical, so the particle oscillates vertically, along the length or axis of the tube.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the air particle oscillates vertically, along the length or along the axis of the tube.

hints: Locate both air particles relative to the node at the midpoint of the tube.
Particles in the same loop of a stationary wave oscillate in phase.
walkthrough: The particles at h = 0.10 m and h = 0.20 m are both in the lower loop, between the bottom antinode and the node at h = 0.30 m.
All particles in the same stationary-wave loop oscillate in phase.
The phase difference is 0°.
State 0° as the phase difference.

hints: The two antinodes at the open ends are adjacent antinodes, so the tube length is half a wavelength.
Find the wavelength from the 0.60 m tube length, then rearrange v = fλ for frequency.
walkthrough: The antinodes at the two open ends are separated by λ / 2.
Therefore 0.60 m = λ / 2, so λ = 1.20 m.
Use v = fλ, giving f = v / λ = 340 / 1.20 = 283... Hz.
To two significant figures, the frequency is 280 Hz.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses λ = 2 × 0.60 m and obtains a frequency of 280 Hz.

hints: The next stationary-wave mode in an open–open tube has one complete wavelength across the tube length.
Use the unchanged sound speed with this shorter wavelength in v = fλ.
walkthrough: For the next allowed mode, the 0.60 m tube contains one complete wavelength.
Thus λ = 0.60 m.
To two significant figures, the next stationary-wave frequency is 570 Hz.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses a wavelength of 0.60 m for the next mode and obtains 570 Hz.
